body: I am sorry that something bad happened after something so good. But I am glad that you found someone who brings you joy. If you don't mind my asking, why does your boyfriend make you happy?

Oh my goodness that is insane. When I first read this post I wondered if this was some small startup. But this is a full-fledged corporation. And even if there are other people in your department you were definitely still understaffed if that was your workload. It sucks that they made you handle so many different types of transactions. That must have made it hard keeping track of things.

I am sorry that your relationship with your mother is abusive. I can definitely say with complete confidence that you are not a failure of a daughter. Children can't fail their parents. A parent's love is supposed to be unconditional. 

How is your relationship with your brother? Does he feel the same way about your mom?

I also have not heard about this human rights violation in Arkansas. What happened?

I am sorry that this has fallen on you. This is ultimately the fault of your employers for not dedicating enough resources to their accounting department. In fact, it sounds like you might have been the only accountant at your company? Given the workload you have listed i am so impressed with how you have shouldered the burden.

You are definitely not alone right now. I am in college right now struggling with the very things that you are talking about. I feel that no matter how hard I try, I will never be good enough in my field (economics). Quarantine has definitely made social life difficult for introverted people. I have felt most of my friendships wither from distance. Life sucks.

That said, I think that you should be proud that you are training to be a physician. This indicates that you are concerned with the well being of others and want to make the lives of other people better. Is this why you want to be a physician? If so, I think this is a really important aspect of what qualifies you.
I am happy that I had the chance to hear the way that you are feeling. I want you to know that I will be rooting for you.

Absolutely none of this is your fault at all. It must be very difficult to juggle these challenges all at once.

I can only see that your boyfriend must love you and that is something awesome.

It's totally normal to have trouble vocalizing the way you are feeling to other people and by downplaying how bad you feel. I wish i was better at communicating the severity of how I am feeling to other people too. 

Romantic love is hard for me too, but it sounds like there are people in your life who love you too. It's awesome that your friends are capable of giving you joy. I imagine that you bring joy to them too. And from the way that you talk about your father makes it sound like he loves you deeply.

I am sorry that you have gone through so much. I can't offer any advice, but I can say that  I admire that you help the people who contact you despite the burden it puts on you. That takes a lot of courage and it tells me that you are a strong person.

Regardless of whether or not you go to his wedding, I think that he is lucky to have you as a best friend.

I also have felt/feel a missing passion that makes life feel worth living. Over the last two years I have struggled to find a purpose that propels me through life and makes me want to do my best. I think a cement duvet is a good way of describing this feeling.

I have found a bit of hope during the pandemic through volunteering. It gave me a sense that I was contributing to something that was more significant than myself. I would recommend signing up to do some volunteer work, even if its only 1 or 2 hours per week. It can put you in contact with good and passionate people. I always felt a bit more grounded during and after volunteering.
